newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaireans adjourn peace talks in South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans adjourn peace talks in South Africa.

text.p: Zaire's warring sides said on Tuesday after peace talks in South Africa that they had agreed on the need for a ceasefire but gave no details of how this could be implemented.
Delegates representing President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila adjourned their negotiations on Tuesday four days after meeting for the first time in Pretoria.
"Both parties agreed on negotiations to bring about a peaceful, political solution to the conflict," a joint statement said.
"This necessitates a complete cessation of hostilities and other measures consistent with the implementation of the U.N.- OAU peace plan," said the statement, issued at a news conference.
The Zaireans left the news conference in Pretoria without taking questions. It was not immediately clear if they were heading back to Zaire.

South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who convened the talks along with Mohamed Sahnoun, representative of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity, told the news conference the Zaireans needed to consult their leaders.
"A spirit of mutual trust is developing...they are adjourning to allow the parties to consult their principals," Mbeki said.
He said the parties had discussed the "timing and modalities" of a ceasefire.
